about: A command line interface for Capsule - the photo management platform
long_about:
Capsule CLI provides tools for managing your photos and albums:

- Authentication management
- Sync local and remote data
- Check status and list files
- Manage albums and collections

subcommands.about: Hand uploads to another device of this account, or upload ones handed to this device
subcommands.name: peer

subcommands.about: Take hand-off files another device of this account sealed for this one, then upload every hand-off this device holds under its own session, deleting each copy once the server holds it. A hand-off that can never succeed is quarantined: kept, not retried, listed by `capsule peer status` and deleted only by `capsule peer discard`

args.help: Path to this device's Capsule library
A hand-off file to take (repeatable); without one, only the held hand-offs upload

Also take hand-offs over the LAN peering channel: listen on ADDR (e.g. `0.0.0.0:7420`) for the other device's `capsule peer delegate --peer`, verify it over mutual TLS as a device of this account, pull each hand-off it sealed for this device, and acknowledge each over the same channel once it is persisted. Only local-network peers are admitted. The address bound is printed on stderr
Seconds `--listen` waits for a peer to connect and verify; a verified session is not cut by it, but runs to its end at a minimum transfer rate
Open the tier sessions in ladder order, gating the above-index tiers on the connection class, as `capsule push --staged` does
Read the library passphrase from stdin instead of prompting, so the command works in scripts and CI where there is no terminal

Print the run as one JSON document on stdout: each hand-off taken with its acknowledgement (and, over the channel, the peer it came from and whether the peer took the acknowledgement), each refused, and what became of each held hand-off (removed, kept, failed and kept, or permanently refused and quarantined), each failure with a stable `kind`, the server's `code` when it gave one, and the detail

subcommands.name: accept

subcommands.about: Seal assets' uploads for another device of this account to upload later. Each asset is written to a hand-off file the other device takes with `capsule peer accept`, or with `--peer` handed over the LAN peering channel to `capsule peer accept --listen`; this device keeps every original until its own check finds the server holds it

args.help: Path to the Capsule library holding the assets
The device to hand the uploads to: its id in this account's device directory. Required with `--out`; with `--peer`, the device the channel verifies must be this one
An asset to hand off (repeatable)
Directory the hand-off files are written to

Hand the uploads over the LAN peering channel instead of files: dial the other device's `capsule peer accept --listen` at HOST:PORT, verify it over mutual TLS as a device of this account, and serve it each hand-off to pull and acknowledge over the same channel. Only a local-network address is dialed
Hours to wait for the server to hold the assets before taking the uploads back
Read the library passphrase from stdin instead of prompting, so the command works in scripts and CI where there is no terminal

Print the run as one JSON document on stdout: the delegate, each asset handed off, with its file or whether the delegate acknowledged it over the channel, and its content address, and each that was not, with a stable `kind`, the server's `code` when it gave one, and the detail

Read the library passphrase from stdin instead of prompting, so the command works in scripts and CI where there is no terminal
Print the discarded hand-off as one JSON document on stdout: its content address, its asset and the `kind` it had been quarantined for

subcommands.name: discard

subcommands.about: Send this library's assets to another device of this account over the LAN peering channel: dial its `capsule peer pull --listen`, verify it over mutual TLS as a device of this account, and serve it one backup artifact sealed for that session. The other device skips what it already holds and refuses what it has purged

args.help: Path to the Capsule library holding the assets
The other device's `capsule peer pull --listen` address. Only a local-network address is dialed
The device the channel must verify; refused if the device at `--peer` is another
An asset to send (repeatable); without one, every asset in the library is sent
Read the library passphrase from stdin instead of prompting, so the command works in scripts and CI where there is no terminal

Print the run as one JSON document on stdout: the device the channel verified, the artifact's content address, size and assets, how many bytes the other device pulled, and each failure with a stable `kind` and the detail

subcommands.name: offer

subcommands.about: Take assets another device of this account sends with `capsule peer offer`: listen on ADDR, verify the device over mutual TLS, pull its backup artifact and write every asset that is new or a forward update. An asset this device has purged is refused, and the run is refused before listening if the purge record cannot be read

args.help: Path to this device's Capsule library
The address to listen on (e.g. `0.0.0.0:7420`). Only local-network peers are admitted. The address bound is printed on stderr
Seconds to wait for a peer to connect and verify; a verified session is not cut by it, but runs to its end at a minimum transfer rate
Read the library passphrase from stdin instead of prompting, so the command works in scripts and CI where there is no terminal

Print the run as one JSON document on stdout: the peer, each artifact pulled, the assets `applied`, `quarantined` (the peer sent stale state), `tombstoned` (purged here), `identical` (already held) and `incomplete`, each failure and each refused connection with a stable `kind` and the detail

subcommands.name: pull

subcommands.about: Show this device's handed-off assets: take the other device's acknowledgements, take back uploads that are overdue or whose device was revoked, and release what the server holds. A delete made after a hand-off is held until the server holds the asset, then sent. Also lists every hand-off this device quarantined

args.help: Path to the Capsule library holding the assets
An acknowledgement file `capsule peer accept` wrote (repeatable)
Read the library passphrase from stdin instead of prompting, so the command works in scripts and CI where there is no terminal

Print the run as one JSON document on stdout: each delegation with its state, each refused acknowledgement with a stable `kind` and the detail, each quarantined hand-off with its file, the stable `kind` of its refusal, the server's `code` when it gave one, and the detail, and each delete made after a hand-off with the records between the hand-off and it (held, sent, failed and kept, or refused and not retried)
